result: I concluded that the uncoordinated 2-aminothiophenol molecule is disordered over two positions, and I submitted a two-part model for it. The original model had a 2.4 e/Å³ difference peak 1.4 Å from S4 and a −2.0 hole, and S4's displacement ellipsoid was badly stretched (Ueq 0.23, anisotropy 8). The peak sat exactly where the S atom would be if the whole molecule were rotated about 30° in its ring plane. I modelled the existing molecule as PART 1 and a matching copy in that rotated orientation as PART 2, with their occupancies tied to one free variable. Both parts have riding hydrogens and are held in shape by SADI/FLAT geometry restraints and RIGU/SIMU displacement restraints. Occupancies refined to 0.56/0.44, R1 fell from 0.0611 to 0.0531 and wR2 from 0.141 to 0.125, and the residual map is flat (largest peak 1.2, deepest hole −1.1 e/Å³). The minor-part atoms are isotropic: refining them anisotropically made the model unstable. Three minor ring carbons (C55–C57), which overlap the major ring, have their Uiso fixed at 0.09, close to the major ring's values. Nothing else in the structure was changed.
